title: A moving rod, measured at one time
spoken: Simultaneous moving-rod length is rest length over gamma.
explanation: Locating both ends of a moving rod at the same time in the stationary system gives its rest length divided by gamma. At 0.6c a 1 m rod measures 0.8 m.
assumptions: A clock and a rod at rest in the moving system, which moves at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c.
The clock's two ticks happen at the same place in its own rest frame; the rod's two ends are located at the same time in the stationary system.
Modern teaching notation: Delta tau is the modern proper time, the time one clock records. It is not the paper's tau, which is the moving system's time coordinate.

notes.title: Rest length over gamma
notes.explanation: Gamma is at least 1, so the measured length is never longer than the rest length.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: The result of one stated measurement procedure. Locate the two ends at different times and the number is different; that is a different measurement, not a different rod.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared: 1 at rest, larger at any speed, without limit as v approaches c. The paper writes it as beta.

notes.title: Length of the moving rod
notes.explanation: The distance between where the two ends are at one time of the stationary system.

notes.title: Rest length
notes.explanation: The length a ruler at rest with the rod gives.
